stem:
Sonia writes $24=8\times 3$ and $36=9\times 4$. She asks whether that single pair of factorisations proves that $24$ and $36$ have no common factor greater than $1$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Yes, because those written factor pairs show no matching factor on the page.
No, because another factorisation can still reveal a common factor such as $12$.
The numbers share a factor only after she first concludes they are co-prime.
The same single-pair check also settles every later prime-factorisation question about these numbers.

teacher.key_rationale: One chosen factorisation can miss a shared factor. Here 24=12×2 and 36=12×3, so 12 is common. Matching factors on one writing is not a full search. Sharing a factor only after a co-prime conclusion reverses the logic. A single pair does not replace later prime-factor work.
